In August 2024, there were 41 fatal workplace accidents in Shanghai with 41 deaths.
On August 6, an accident happened in the factory of Shanghai Jiahao Printing Machinery Co., Ltd. at No.363, Lianda Road.
An operator who was renovating a roof fell through a hole onto the ground and died.
On August 10, an accident happened in Shanghai Changjiu Logistics Co., Ltd. at No.18, Lane 1750, Luchaogang Road.
A reach stacker was lowering down a container, which hit and killed an operator standing underneath the container.
On August 13, an accident happened in Shanghai Longxian Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd. at Room 103, Floor 1, Building 26, No.208, Jinyuanwu Road.
An operator was moving goods at the mezzanine floor in the warehouse.
The individual fell to the ground and died.
On August 13, an accident happened at No.236, Forte Land Ailunpo Complex.
An operator commissioned by Huzhou Yuanpai Window and Door Technology Co., Ltd. was installing a sunroom at the property.
The individual fell off from the roof and died.
On August 29, an accident happened at the project site of Lane 135, Shangzhong Road W.
A steel sheet on the ground became tangled in an excavator's treads.
An operator standing on the sheet fell down and was hit by the bounced-up sheet.
The individual died.
At 9:53 pm, an accident happened at a room of No.1376, Nanjing Road W.
An operator of a Shanghai construction and decoration company was connecting wires in a dropped ceiling.
The individual had an electric shock and died.
The operator lacked safety awareness and did not have an electrician certificate.
The individual did not shut down the power during the wire connecting operation.
The operator had a contact with the live wire and was killed.
The company did not fulfill its safety responsibilities.
Its work safety condition did not meet the national standards or industry requirements.
It took up decoration projects beyond its qualification and promised to undertake maintenance and repairment obligations.
It assigned an unqualified operator to the electrician’s work.
It did not hold safety education or training among its operators.
The project owner is a Shanghai medical technology company.
It did not fulfill its safety responsibilities either.
It fabricated materials and provided false materials to apply for a construction permit.
It commissioned the decoration project and its maintenance works to an unqualified vendor.
During the dangerous electrician work, it did not assign a dedicated safety supervisor to the job site.
It did not ensure standard operating procedures had been followed and safety measures have been taken.
Jingan District Emergency Management Bureau imposed administrative penalties upon the two companies and their leaders.
Both companies should thoroughly learn from this accident and fulfill their safety responsibilities.
The construction and decoration company should operate strictly according to Chinese laws and regulations and stop taking up projects it was not qualified for.
Specialized jobs must be carried out only by license holders.
It should require its employees to follow standard operating procedures to effectively protect their life safety and avoid accidents from happening again.
The medical technology company should strictly follow Chinese laws and regulations to rectify its project commissioning process.
It should stop cheating in its operations and fulfill its obligations to ensure work safety.
At about 9:40 am on August 5, 2023, an accident happened at No.1089, Dongdaming Road.
An operator from a Shanghai construction and decoration company was standing on a foldable ladder to check the air conditioner duct.
The individual fell to the ground and died in a hospital after rescuing attempts failed.
The operator was not wearing a safety helmet and was using a defective ladder with damaged feet.
The individual lost balance while working about 1.9 to 2.3 meters in the air and fell to the ground.
The company did not provide the operator with a tool that met national standards.
The ladder was missing its anti-slip pads, which was not allowed according to China’s Safety Standard for Portable Metal Ladders (GB/T 27685-2019).
It stipulated that the ladder's anti-slip units shall be replaced or restored in the event of wear, damage or loss.
The company did not provide its employees with personal protective equipment and did not require or educate them to wear or use helmets.
The company did not fulfill its work safety responsibilities and did not design and implement an internal safety accountability system.
Since it undertook the project in September 2022, it did not require the project team to set up and implement customized internal safety rules and guidelines.
It did not hold safety training among the job site managers and did not assign personnel to patrol the site.
The project manager lacked safety awareness and was careless in hiring workers.
The manager did not hold effective trainings and failed to manage the process.
After the accident happened, the team on the site did not report the mishap as required by regulations.
The deceased operator lacked safety awareness, ignored the hazards of this job, and was not wearing a helmet.
Judicial authorities are pursuing criminal liabilities of the job site manager assigned by the construction and decoration company.
Hongkou District Emergency Management Bureau imposed administrative penalties upon the company and its leader.
The company should thoroughly learn from this accident, identify its root causes, and implement effective corrective measures.
Its leader should take up its legal responsibilities for work safety as well as develop and implement its internal safety rules and guidelines.
It should enhance its human resource management and provide more rigorous safety trainings.
It should improve its work in identifying and mitigating safety hazards.
The property management team must ensure that all contractors and tenants are qualified and adhere to strict safety standards.
They should also monitor their safety practices closely.
If a contractor or tenant fails a safety evaluation, they will be required to make immediate improvements.
Persistent safety violations may result in the termination of their contracts.
To ensure the work safety in the shopping complex, the property management team, contractors, and tenants must strictly adhere to their safety obligations as outlined in their agreements.
The various departments of the property management company should coordinate better to fulfill their responsibilities and holistically supervise the safety measures.
Businesses should provide better safety education for their employees, temporary workers and contracted workers.
To ensure the safety of temporary workers with limited education, high turnover, and short hours, safety training must be tailored and impactful.
This training should focus on enhancing their awareness, skills, and ability to respond effectively to emergencies.
The authority in charge of relevant industries should thoroughly evaluate and learn from this accident to ensure rigorous corrective actions have been taken.
The lessons learned should be widely disseminated to ensure accountability at all levels.
While growth is important, it must never come at the expense of safety.
Authorities should review their responsibilities carefully to avoid neglecting their safety obligations.
They should focus on the development and implementation of safety rules and regulations as well as improve their routine supervision works.
The neighborhood committee should take up their responsibilities to enhance safety management within their jurisdiction, especially checking businesses’ operating processes.

They should stick to the requirements of the Standards for Identifying Major Accident Hazards in Industrial and Commercial Enterprises to identify hazards and focus on relevant companies to take preventive measures.
They should require businesses to fulfill their obligations and proactively take actions.
If there are conditions that they could not handle, they should report the cases to relevant authorities.
Organizers and space owners of events with large gatherings must fulfill their obligations in safety management, evacuation organization and warnings.
They must set up conspicuous safety signs and keep safety exits and evacuation paths clear.
They must design emergency plans and maintain order at the event.
Large crowds must be well managed and quickly evacuated in case of emergency.
Upon entering crowded spaces, the public should pay attention to safety signs and the location of exits to avoid crowd rush accidents.
People should pay attention to traffic safety, especially at roads near scenic spots.
Arterial roads will experience higher traffic.

Drivers must actively uphold traffic laws and refrain from dangerous behaviors, including: yielding improperly, changing lanes illegally, driving under the influence of alcohol, driving without a license, failing to keep safe distance, driving backward illegally, cycling against traffic, and disregarding traffic signals.
Industrial trading companies and those handling hazardous chemicals must rigorously identify and address all potential risks.
Strict controls must be in place for all sources of dangers.
Adequate staffing, including managers, should be ensured during holidays.
Reasonable work schedule and shift arrangements should be made to ensure safe operations.

Businesses and organizations involved in travel activities, such as scenic spots, travel agencies, heritage sites, museums, commercial transportation and cruises, must conduct a thorough hazard assessment prior to the holiday break.
Particular attention should be given to inspecting electrical systems, gas lines, fire safety equipment, crowd control measures and entertainment facilities.
Clear safety signage and educational materials should be prominently displayed to guide visitors.
For activities involving camping or open fires, strict adherence to fire safety regulations is essential to prevent accidents.
